title: 4053. Minimum Operations to Make Every Element Palindromic

examples.explanation: One optimal sequence of operations is: Decrement nums[0] by 2 once to change it from 10 to 8. Decrement nums[1] by 2 twice to change it from 12 to 8. Decrement nums[2] by 2 three times to change it from 14 to 8. Increment nums[3] by 2 three times to change it from 16 to 22. After 1 + 2 + 3 + 3 = 9 operations, nums = [8, 8, 8, 22], and every element is a positive palindromic integer. It can be shown that fewer than 9 operations cannot achieve this.

Decrement nums[1] and nums[3] by 2 once each. After 2 operations, nums = [9, 8, 11, 8], and every element is a positive palindromic integer. At least one operation is needed for each of these two elements, so the minimum number of operations is 2.

Decrement nums[0] by 2 twice to change it from 125 to 121, which is a positive palindromic integer. A single operation would change it to 123 or 127, neither of which is palindromic. Thus, the minimum number of operations is 2.
